answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a onyx as the anchor of the cost.
